title: Containerize: one image, one compose file, one health check

concept.heading: A container is the runnable artifact a client can start without you
paragraphs: Everything so far runs from your terminal with uv. A client's server does not have your terminal. A Docker image packages the Python version, the locked dependencies and the code into one artifact that starts the same way everywhere; a compose file names the services around it (the CRM mock for demos, a volume for state, an optional trace UI) and how they connect. docker compose up is the whole install.

Three details separate a demo image from a deployable one. Copy the lock file and install dependencies before copying the code, so a code change does not reinstall the world. Run as a non-root user. Give the orchestrator a HEALTHCHECK that hits /health, so a crashed server is restarted and a half-started one is not sent traffic.

State lives in a volume under /data, never inside the container; an image is replaced on every update and must not carry the approvals queue with it. Secrets arrive as environment variables from the platform, never baked into the image.
concept.lowCodeEquivalent: Exporting a managed solution and importing it in the client's environment, with connection references supplied there. The image is the solution; the compose file is the environment; the env vars are the connection references.

pythonBlock.title: Python you need: a health route on the Starlette app, PORT from the environment
pythonBlock.intro: The SDK lets you add plain HTTP routes next to /mcp. A health route that does not touch the CRM is what the orchestrator polls.
pythonBlock.code:
from starlette.responses import JSONResponse

@server.custom_route("/health", methods=["GET"])
async def health(request):
    return JSONResponse({"status": "ok", "service": "lakeshore-donor-ops"})

# Dockerfile sketch
# FROM python:3.11-slim
# COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:latest /uv /usr/local/bin/uv
# WORKDIR /app
# COPY pyproject.toml uv.lock ./
# RUN uv sync --frozen --no-dev --extra mcp --extra otel --extra rag
# COPY . .
# RUN useradd -m app && chown -R app /app && mkdir -p /data && chown app /data
# USER app
# ENV PORT=8080 STATE_DB=/data/state.db
# HEALTHCHECK --interval=15s --timeout=3s CMD python -c "import urllib.request,os; urllib.request.urlopen(f'http://127.0.0.1:{os.environ.get(\"PORT\",\"8080\")}/health')"
# CMD ["uv", "run", "--no-sync", "python", "-m", "mcp_server.http_server"]

spec: Add the /health route and make the HTTP server bind 0.0.0.0 when HOST is set (containers need it).

Write compose.yaml with the middleware and crm services, the state volume, env from .env, and an optional trace-ui under a profile.
docker compose up --build, wait for healthy, then run the Module 2 HTTP check against http://127.0.0.1:8080/mcp with a token. Set DOCKER_AVAILABLE=1 and run this lesson's check.

check.summary: The Dockerfile has the required shape (slim base, lock-first uv sync, non-root, HEALTHCHECK on /health, runs the HTTP server); compose declares middleware and crm with port 8080, a /data volume and a healthcheck; with DOCKER_AVAILABLE=1, compose up reaches healthy and /health answers 200.
